question: I'm following along with this video to install a Thunderbolt card in my Dell Precision Tower 7910. Please guide me through each step as it happens.

ground_truth.response: Start by powering off your computer and unplugging the power cable from the back for safety.
Next, pull the latch on the side of the chassis and lift the panel off to open the tower.
Release the blue latch for slot three and remove the metal slot cover to prepare for the card installation.
Carefully align the Thunderbolt card with slot three, push it in until it clicks, and close the blue latch to secure it.
Now connect the internal cables: plug the small connector into the motherboard and route the other cable through the guide to its header.
Once the internal cables are secure, slide the side panel back onto the chassis until it locks into place.
Finally, plug the DisplayPort and Thunderbolt cables into the corresponding ports on the back of the newly installed card.

question: I'm using this video to plant some trees in my backyard. Please guide me through each step as it happens.

ground_truth.response: Find a suitable location and space your trees 10 feet apart. Then, use a shovel to mark the ground by tracing around the base of the pot.
Now, dig your hole to the exact depth of the pot. You can use a jackhammer if the soil is too hard for a standard shovel.
Widen the hole until it is twice the diameter of the pot, approximately 24 inches across. This ensures the roots have space to expand.
Add some planting mix and fertilizer into the hole. Use your shovel to mix them thoroughly with the soil at the bottom.
ground_truth.event_description: Preparing the soil in the hole

ground_truth.response: Remove the tree from its plastic pot and drop it into the center of the hole. Make sure it is positioned upright.
Shovel soil back into the hole around the root ball. Level it by hand, then use your feet to firmly compact the dirt.
Build a small earthen wall around the tree to create a water basin. Add a bit more planting mix and fertilizer inside the ring.
Finally, thoroughly water your tree with a hose. Fill the basin at the base first, then spray down the leaves.

question: I'm following along to make this paper windmill fan. Please guide me through each step as it happens.

ground_truth.response: Start with a square paper. Use a ruler and pencil to mark the diagonal creases from each corner towards the center, stopping before you reach the middle.
Use scissors to cut along those diagonal lines from each corner. Be careful to stop at the marks you made earlier so the center remains intact.
Apply glue to the center. Fold every other corner of the flaps into the middle and press firmly to secure them, forming the windmill blades.
Now, take a rectangular piece of paper and roll it tightly from one corner into a thin tube. Secure the edge with a bit of glue.
Finally, poke a hole through the center of the windmill and the top of the handle. Use a pin to join the two pieces together.
